title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Occupancy Period, Lender and Seller Charge Limits and Appraisal Validity
content:
The VA Home Loan Guaranty fixes, per program, the calendar days after closing within which the veteran must occupy the home, the longest delayed occupancy accepted with a documented reason, the maximum flat origination fee a lender may charge (percent of the loan amount), the maximum seller concessions (percent of the reasonable value), the most energy efficient improvements that may be added to the loan without a new appraisal, and the calendar days a VA appraisal remains valid for a loan to close.

## Limits by program

| Program | Occupy within (calendar days of closing) | Longest documented delay (months) | Origination fee at most (% of loan amount) | Seller concessions at most (% of reasonable value) | Energy efficient improvements without a new appraisal (USD) | Appraisal valid for (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| VA Manufactured Home Loan | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| VA Purchase Loan (10% or More Down) | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| VA Purchase Loan (5% to Less Than 10% Down) | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| VA Purchase Loan (Less Than 5% Down) | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| VA Cash-Out Refinance Loan | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |
| Native American Direct Loan (NADL) | 60 | 12 | 1.0 | 4.0 | 6000.00 | 180 |

## Hypothetical illustration

On a hypothetical loan amount of 300,000.00 dollars, a flat origination fee may be at most 300,000.00 multiplied by 1.0 and divided by one hundred, or 3,000.00 dollars. On a hypothetical reasonable value of 310,000.00 dollars, seller concessions may be at most 310,000.00 multiplied by 4.0 and divided by one hundred, or 12,400.00 dollars.
